mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thus producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the trigger, with p-value > 0.05 in a two-tailed test versus pre-tightening periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly pay growth acceleration (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% above the prior month's rate signals labor market strength, which is associated with higher consumer confidence and thus positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly growth rate > previous month + 0.5%
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, returns underperform a 0.5% PAYEMS growth baseline (mean difference < -0.2% with p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both GDP demand proxy GDPC1 and retail sales proxy HOUST over two consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it indicates sustained consumer and business demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both increase month-over-month for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Economic expansion with rising consumption and production
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative or flat despite the dual series moving higher (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) index below 102.0 signals supply-side weakness, lowering market confidence and producing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
regime_hint: Supply shock or soft landing risk
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive or indistinguishable from baseline during INDPRO contraction (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, prompting the Fed to hold rates steady and supporting equity valuations, thus positive 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 3.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite UNRATE staying below 3.5% for the trigger period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the consumer price index inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3.0% signals disinflation, reducing rate hike expectations and supporting equity valuations, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns underperform a 3.0% CPIAUCSL baseline (mean difference < -0.1%, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both retail sales (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 2% in the same month suggests robust demand, which is associated with higher 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both increase by ≥2% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative or flat despite both proxies rising by ≥2% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS below 4.00% over the prior quarter is interpreted as persistent policy easing, which is expected to drive positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative or flat despite the 3-month FEDFUNDS MA being below 4.00% (p > 0.05).
